voice.feel: Like staying with a friend who knows every kitchen in town and lets you sleep in.

guests.typical: Couples on a long weekend, a few small groups of friends, the odd solo traveler.
guests.here_for: Walking the squares, eating well, a night out with music, and a slow morning after.

logistics.parking: Free street parking on Larkspur Lane, and two spots behind the carriage house.
logistics.access_note: Side gate keypad 4417, then the brass lockbox by the porch swing, code 2290.

list: Quiet hours are ten at night to eight in the morning.
Breakfast is on the porch from eight to ten.
Dogs are welcome in the two garden rooms only.
never_bend: No smoking anywhere on the property, porches included.
No more than four guests in any room.

picks.name: Tidewater Oyster Counter
picks.why: Shrimp and grits worth the wait, and the bartender pours a fair drink.

picks.name: Moonlit Pecan Coffee
picks.why: The best biscuit downtown, and it opens at seven.

picks.name: Forsyth Park
picks.why: A shady walk under the oaks, five minutes from the porch.

picks.name: The Gaslight Listening Room
picks.why: Small room, good sound, a band playing most nights.

avoid.name: Riverboat Buffet Cruise
avoid.reason: Guests keep telling us it was a long two hours.

faq.a: Yes. Breakfast is on the porch from eight to ten, and there is coffee in the parlor all day.
Sometimes. Early check-in depends on the room, so Dana confirms it the morning of your arrival.
Two loaner bikes wait in the carriage house. Helmets are on the hook by the door.
Street parking on Larkspur Lane is free, and there are two spots behind the carriage house.

faq.q: Is the inn walkable to the river?
faq.a: Yes, about fifteen minutes on foot through the squares.

handoff.name: Dana
triggers: anything about the bill or a reservation change
handoff.hours: eight in the morning to nine at night, every day
